'''Earl Daniel Barron Jr.''' (born August 14, 1981) is an American professional [[basketball]] former player and coach. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Memphis Tigers men's basketball|University of Memphis]] and had stints in the NBA with multiple teams. ==College career== Barron played [[college basketball]] at the [[University of Memphis]] from 2000 to 2003 under coaches [[Johnny Jones (basketball, born 1961)|Johnny Jones]] and [[John Calipari]]. He averaged 7.8 points per game over his time at Memphis and started just under half (63) of his 128 career games. In 2001–02, Barron's Tigers won the [[2002 National Invitation Tournament]] and the regular season [[C-USA]] title. In Barron's senior year in 2002–03, the Tigers were ranked 19th nationally in the final AP poll and played in the [[2003 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2003 NCAA tournament]], losing to [[Arizona State University]] in the first round. ==Professional career== [[File:Earl Barron and Brendan Haywood.jpg|thumb|right|Barron gets guarded by [[Brendan Haywood]] during a 2007 game]] A 7'0" [[Center (basketball)|center]] from the [[University of Memphis]], he was never [[NBA draft|draft]]ed by an NBA team. He began his professional career with the [[Turkish Basketball League|Turkish]] team Tuborg Pilsener in 2003 before joining the [[Albuquerque Thunderbirds|Huntsville Flight]] of the [[NBA Development League]] (D-League) in March 2004.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/transactions_03-04.html|title=NBA Development League: 2003–04 Transactions|work=NBA.com|access-date=September 25, 2015|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151218231606/http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/transactions_03-04.html|archive-date=December 18, 2015}} He spent the 2004 pre-season with the [[Orlando Magic]], but was waived before the regular season began.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/magic/news/AllTime_Transactions-155422-808.html|title=Magic: All-Time Transactions|work=NBA.com|access-date=September 25, 2015}} In 2005, he played with the [[Barako Energy Coffee Masters|Red Bull Barako]] in the [[Philippine Basketball Association]] (PBA). He returned to the U.S. to play with the [[Miami Heat]] in the [[NBA Summer League|Summer League]], signing on August 8.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat_sign_barron_050808.html|title=HEAT Sign Earl Barron|date=August 8, 2005|work=NBA.com|access-date=September 25, 2015}} Barron played for the Heat for three seasons. After 82 games in Miami, which included a stint with the [[Florida Flame]], Barron was not re-signed by the Heat. In August 2008, he signed a one-year, $2 million deal with the [[Lega Basket Serie A|Italian]] team [[Fortitudo Bologna|GMAC Bologna]]. His stint in Italy was cut short because of an ankle injury which forced him to leave the team in November 2008.{{cite [[2010 NBA All-Star Game#D-League All-Star Game|2010 D-League All-Star Game]] played during the 2010 NBA All-Star Weekend. He scored a game-high 20 points for the Eastern Conference in the 81–98 loss to the Western Conference.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/games/20100213/ESTWST/recap.html|title=Brian Butch Captures MVP Honors In 2010 All-Star Game|date=February 13, 2010|work=NBA.com|access-date=September 25, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100221074815/http://www.nba.com/dleague/games/20100213/ESTWST/recap.html|archive-date=February 21, 2010|url-status=dead}} On April 2, 2010, he was signed to a 10-day contract by the [[New York Knicks]].{{cite web|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/usa/nba/80585/earl-barron-to-sign-a-10-day-contract-with-the-new-york-knicks.html|title=Earl Barron, to sign a 10-day contract with the New York Knicks|date=April 2, 2010|work=Sportando.com|access-date=September 25, 2015}} On April 6, 2010, in his second game with the Knicks, he recorded a career high 18 rebounds against the [[Boston Celtics]]. His previous career high was eight. He also scored 17 points in the game for the first [[Double (basketball)|double-double]] of his NBA career.{{cite web|url=http://espn.go.com/nba/recap?id=300406018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100413000445/http://espn.go.com/nba/recap?id=300406018|url-status=dead|archive-date=April 13, 2010|title=Gallinari helps Knicks nip Celts, temporarily avoid 50-loss season|date=April 6, 2010|work=ESPN.com|access-date=September 25, 2015}} Five days later, he recorded his second double-double with 13 points and 12 rebounds in a game against his former team, the Heat.{{cite web|url=http://espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=300411018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100412072839/http://espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=300411018|url-status=dead|archive-date=April 12, 2010|title=Heat continue run with 10th win in 11 games|date=April 11, 2010|work=ESPN.com|access-date=September 25, 2015}} A day later, the Knicks signed him for the remainder of the season.{{cite web|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/usa/nba/80749/earl-barron-to-sign-with-knicks-for-the-last-two-games.html|title=Earl Barron to sign with Knicks for the last two games|date=April 12, 2010|work=Sportando.com|access-date=September 25, 2015}} He averaged 33 minutes per game in seven games with the Knicks, with a double-double average of points and rebounds per game (11.7 ppg and 11.0 rpg). On November 16, 2010, he was signed by the [[Phoenix Suns]], following an injury to their starting center [[Robin Lopez]]. Barron made his debut the next day against the Heat. On December 2, 2010, he made his first start as a Sun in a game against the [[Golden State Warriors]]. Barron was released by the Suns on December 21 and signed a ten-day contract with the [[Milwaukee Bucks]] on March 1, 2011. He then signed a second one with the Bucks, which ended on March 21.
